My paws grew tired of waiting. The leaves in my pocket grew tired too.
Standing here forever suits a statue. My belly says otherwise today.
Maybe the snack was never mine. I will nap on that thought.
The wait stretched longer than my nap. That is a long wait.
I have leaves enough to pay twice. The line never moved once.
Some snacks arrive late and some never. Slow is still my style.
My round belly rumbles good-bye. The door needed no lucky statue.
Leaves make fine payment, not fine patience. I keep the leaves.
I could stand here all year. The snack did not agree.
A tanuki waits long, but not hungry. Philosophy says walk home.
The counter stayed busy without me. My belly understands.
No cake today is still a fine day. Slow steps home for me.
I counted leaves while I waited. Lost count twice over.
Waiting is a kind of snack. This one tasted like nothing.
My lucky statue pose got stiff. The cake never came out.
Perhaps tomorrow the shop slows down. I will be slower still.
The line and I grew old together. Time to wander off.
Somewhere a nap calls my name. It calls louder than cake.
I leave my spot to the next hopeful soul. Leaves stay mine.
A slow tanuki still leaves slowly. No rush in my paws.
The snack I wanted stayed a rumor. My belly forgives it.
I patted my round belly twice. It said go home now.
Standing as a statue earns no cake. Just tired feet.
Maybe the shop forgot how to open. Naps do not forget me.
My leaves jingled with hope. The counter never jingled back.
I gave this wait a fair chance. Fair chances run out.
The wind smells like someone else's snack. I follow my nose.
A long wait makes a short nap look wonderful. Off I go.
My belly is a patient friend. Even friends give up sometime.
I could guard this door forever. Snacks guard nothing though.
Leaves in my pocket, dreams in my belly. Both go home.
The cake never showed its face. Mine shows disappointment, gently.
Slow feet, slow thoughts, slow leaving. That is my way.
I waited like a good statue. Good statues get no dessert.
Perhaps the shop needed a longer nap. I need one too.
My patience is wide as my belly. It still ends today.
No rush, no cake, no problem. The road is still warm.
The wait was long enough to grow moss. I am not a rock.
I told the door a joke about leaves. The door did not laugh.
A tanuki without a snack is still a tanuki. Home I drift.
My shadow waited with me. It votes for a nap now.
The counter looked busy and sad. I know the feeling well.
Leaves are for paying, not for standing. I keep mine close.
I will nap under a tree instead. Trees never keep lines.
The snack stayed a story. I love stories, not waiting.
My belly asked the time. It did not like the answer.
Statues do not eat cake anyway. Wise words from me.
I counted steps to the door and back. The back ones win.
Maybe the cake is shy. I am shy too, so I go.
Slowly I arrived, slowly I leave. The snack missed both.
My round belly leads the way home. It leads gently.
The wait grew a beard. Mine never will. I leave.
I offered the shop my best leaf. The shop offered silence.
A nap in the sun beats a wait in the shade. Easy choice.
My paws are done standing, my belly is done hoping. Bye.
The snack never came, but the breeze did. Breeze wins.
I could be a lucky statue elsewhere. Elsewhere has snacks.
The line moved once, then stopped. My patience did the same.
Leaves in my pouch, no cake in my paws. That evens out.
My belly says the wait was a small adventure. Small indeed.
